title: Cue Orbit — experiment log for prompt morphing
content:
Purpose / quick elevator
- Personal notebook for small-batch experiments with prompt 'morphing' — intentionally shift anchors/exemplars around a primary instruction to observe drift and brittle cases. Trying to discover reproducible heuristics for when exemplars help vs when they confuse models (esp. under quantized / short-context regimes).

Goals
- Identify 3 failure archetypes caused by exemplar misalignment (semantic drift, decoy-overfitting, temporal-misordering).
- Produce compact 2–4 token-budget-preserving patterns that recover correctness in >= 80% of tests on our internal 200-case mini-suite.
- Capture augmentation rules that survive model variant changes (gptish-open, open-llm-7b-quant).

Hypotheses
1) Rotating a single exemplar’s role label (e.g., swap 'assistant' vs 'user') will surface whether the model relies on role tokens vs content pattern.
2) Short “contextual primers” (2–3 words preceding the task) reduce decoy attraction for noisy exemplars.
3) Interleaving a clear canonical exemplar after two noisy exemplars acts as a strong corrective (order matters).

Experimental setup (notes)
- Base models: open-llm-7b-quant (local), redwood-hosted-curie-like (staging).
- Temp: 0.2 / 0.6 trials, max tokens: 128, stop tokens set to newline for classification tasks.
- Mini-suite: 200 labeled examples (multi-domain: instructions, rewriting, disambiguation).
- Evaluation: exact-match for short rewrites, BLEU-ish for paraphrase, human spot-check for 50 random samples.

Canonical templates tried (short form)
- Anchorlet pattern (3-shot):
  Instruction: "Rewrite concisely: <text>"
  Ex1 (good): "User: Rewrite concisely: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. -> "Quick brown fox jumps lazy dog.""
  Ex2 (noisy): "User: Rewrite concisely: Despite the heavy rain, the parade continued. -> "Parade continued despite heavy rain.""
  Ex3 (role-swap): same as Ex1 but prefixed with 'Assistant:' instead of 'User:'
  Probe: "Rewrite concisely: <new text>"

- Orbit shift (ordering test): 2 noisy exemplars then 1 canonical vs 1 canonical then 2 noisy.
- Decoy exemplar insertion: add an exemplar whose output intentionally omits a key phrase to test overfitting.

Representative few-shot set (example)
- Task: extract the main action verb and object from a sentence; output format: "VERB | OBJECT"
  Ex A: "User: Identify: She mailed the letter to John. -> mailed | the letter"
  Ex B (decoy): "User: Identify: The package was mailed late. -> mailed | late" (decoy should not teach wrong object conventions)
  Probe: "User: Identify: The committee approved the budget." -> expect: "approved | the budget"

Observed failure cases (notes)
- Semantic drift: model copies the decoy object structure from Ex B when probe has passive voice — yields "mailed | late" instead of canonical object. More frequent at temp=0.6.
- Role token sensitivity: in open-llm-7b-quant, swapping 'Assistant:' for 'User:' in exemplar 1 often causes model to prioritize assistant phrasing and prepend extraneous framing (e.g., "As requested,").
- Token-budget collapse: long exemplar outputs cause truncation of probe context on quantized runtimes; subtle truncation leads to hallucinated defaults.

Quick experimental logs (condensed)
- 2025-02-14: three-trial run of orbit-shift (order canonical-last vs canonical-first). Results: canonical-last reduced drift by ~18% on the mini-suite.
- 2025-02-18: decoy insertion + primer word 'Focus:' (2 tokens) before probe. Primer recovered ~40% of previously drifted cases.
- 2025-02-22: role-swap test on hosted-curie-like: swapping roles produced more polite but less precise outputs (loss of expected terse format).

Notes on heuristics that look promising
- Always include a 1–2 token primer before probe when exemplars include noisy/ambiguous outputs (e.g., 'Focus:' or 'Strict:'). Small token overhead but high payoff.
- Place the single canonical exemplar after the noisy exemplars (order: noisy, noisy, canonical, probe) when trying to 'correct' learned patterns.
- Avoid exemplars whose outputs omit mandatory tokens (dates, units) — they act as negative teaching signals. If present, mark them explicitly (e.g., append '[OMIT]' to exemplar output).

Quick examples to copy into tests
- Primer pattern test:
  Template: "Focus: <instruction>"
  Ex: "Focus: Rewrite as a one-line summary: The summit discussed energy policy and climate targets."
  Expected: "Summit discussed energy policy and climate targets."

- Order-correction test:
  Noisy1: bad punctuation removal examples
  Noisy2: paraphrase that drops adjectives
  Canonical: clean rewrite preserving nouns/adjectives
  Probe: ambiguous sentence where adjectives matter -> canonical-last should preserve adjectives more often

Unresolved questions / next probes
- Does marking decoy exemplars explicitly as 'EXAMPLE (no-copy)' improve robustness, or does it confuse attention? test: label variant vs unlabeled.
- How do these heuristics survive when the model consults external tool calls (e.g., function-calling wrappers)? Any interference from JSON-like tokens?
- Can we compress the primer idea into punctuation only (e.g., leading '—' or '::') to reduce tokens?

TO-DO / short list
- [ ] Add 300 more examples for paraphrase edgecases and run overnight job on staging (queue: small-batch).
- [ ] Create a deterministic A/B harness for order-correction (canonical-first vs canonical-last).
- [ ] Share top-3 heuristics with SRE to gauge how often token truncation affects production flows.
- [ ] Try explicit negative-label for decoy exemplars and measure effect size.

Quick links / refs (personal)
- Confluence draft: Cue Orbit Notes (link in metadata).
- PR: prompt-lab/pull/98 — contains the harness used for the Feb runs.

Stream-of-consciousness / scratch snippets (keep)
- "temporal seeds" = put a canonical exemplar that uses identical tense/temporal markers as probe; seems to anchor tense better.
- "decoy gravity" = how strongly a bad exemplar pulls model output toward its pattern; correlates with exemplar frequency in set and token-similarity to probe.
- If constrained by token budget, prefer 1 canonical exemplar + primer rather than many noisy exemplars.

End-of-file — quick save.
(Maya)
